Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to inspect the rollout’s flow evidence before editing, then the explicitly required `fish-control-primitives` skill to ground the first architecture proposal. I’ll keep all changes inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consider the candidate complete until both evidence files are updated.

The workspace contract confirms that formal CFD must be left to EvE after exit. I’m now anchoring the visual comparison to the sampled scores, observations, metrics, inherited notes, and the common prewarm state before writing the required pre-edit diagnosis.

The visual evidence is unusually consistent: the naive seed makes real upstream progress but turns down and leaves after about 50 time units, while all three positive-bearing mean-curvature variants reverse the useful motion and exit the right boundary in roughly 17–18 units. I’m checking the assigned parent and inherited optimizer notes now to separate a sign/mechanism failure from a mere gain issue.

The shelf’s mean-curvature invariant remains relevant, but the first evaluated generation falsifies its assumed control sign: three independently parameterized implementations all used positive bearing → positive bend and all produced the same immediate right-boundary escape. The next candidate will test the mechanism’s missing semantic piece—a reversed body-frame bearing-to-curvature mapping—without adding unsupported wake-force or route terms. I’m consulting the shelf’s source-family notes now because that turning family informs the edit.

The required pre-edit note is now recorded. The candidate change is deliberately narrow: it keeps the parent’s schema, bounds, oscillator, and posterior lag intact, and reverses only the evidenced bearing-to-curvature semantics so the next CFD result is interpretable.

The durable guidance now records the concrete negative result from all three completed siblings and its applicability boundary; it does not claim anything about this unevaluated candidate. I’m invoking the mandated checker’s three non-CFD checks separately: semantic guidance, executable policy/schema contract, then solver edit boundary.

The guidance check passed. The exact runtime contract command is blocked because this image has no `julia` executable on `PATH` (exit 127); I’m checking the usual local Julia installations before falling back to static schema/sign probes, while keeping that distinction explicit. The remaining mandated boundary check can still run normally.

A local Julia 1.12.6 runtime is available outside `PATH`, so I found a real executable contract path and am rerunning the mandated assertion suite with it now.

The executable contract, schema completeness, opposite-sign mapping, and odd symmetry all pass; the solver boundary also passes. I’m doing the final provenance review against the assigned parent and prefilled evaluated policy, then I’ll rerun the guidance and boundary guards once more after confirming the diffs.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl): reverses the evidenced bearing-to-curvature sign while holding the parent gait and gains fixed.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md): records visual diagnosis, inherited evidence, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md): adds the reusable negative result that all three positive-bearing/positive-curvature variants lost upstream propulsion and exited right within 17–18 time units.

Guidance semantics, Julia policy/schema execution, sign symmetry, and solver boundary checks all pass. No formal CFD was run, per the workspace contract.
